newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end firmer on comm'l bank rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end firmer on comm'l bank rate cut.

text.p: Taiwan share prices on Tuesday closed cautiously higher on news that state-run First Commercial Bank was cutting its prime lending rate, brokers said.
First Bank, one of Taiwan's Big Three banks, said on Tuesday it was cutting its prime rate by 0.05 percentage points to 7.55 percent from 7.60, effective from Tuesday.
The index gained 9.05 points or 0.14 percent at 6,513.73. Turnover was a modest T$32.82 billion.
"Rate cuts helped sentiment, but investors remain cautious -- probably because the domestic economy has not shown apparent recovery," said George Hou of Jardine Fleming Securities.
"Several industries such as personal computers and polyester fibres have shown recovery, but the market has already reflected this fully," said Michael Hung of Nikko Securities.

Investor caution also was spurred by rising levels of margin loans outstanding, which hit a three-month high of T$216.2 billion on Monday, brokers said. Margin loans have risen since a general market recovery began in March, prompting analysts to worry that they may indicate too much speculative buying.
Brokers noted late buying on electronics, which rose 1.23 percent to lead the gains. Megamedia rose the daily seven percent limit to T$35.9. Acer gained 30 cents to T$41.7.
"With the index at comparatively high levels, investors tend to focus buying on sectors like electronics, which are expected to enjoy good prospects in the fourth quarter," Hou said.
Ambassador Hotel rose T$1.9 to T$42.7 on Tuesday on news it would gain some T$1.6 billion in compensation on its victory in a U.S. lawsuit.

Chiao Tung Bank's honeymoon surge began to lose steam. The state-run bank gained T$3.5 to T$70, but did not manage a fourth straight limit-up. Brokers said Chiao Tung, which saw three limit-ups since listing last Wednesday, had now reached its pre-listing grey market price of T$68.
Brokers said they expected a firming trend ahead as foreign funds expected to continue as net buyers.
In September, foreign funds were net buyers of T$10.9 billion in Taiwan equity.
For Wednesday, a 6,480-6,550 range was seen.
